intro: JSON to XML converts a JSON document into formatted XML right in your browser. Keys prefixed with @_ are emitted as XML attributes, and the output is pretty-printed with two-space indentation. It is handy when you need to feed XML-based APIs, configuration files, or legacy systems from data you already have as JSON.
useCases: Transform JSON API responses into XML for systems or services that only accept XML
Generate XML configuration or data files from JSON during development
Produce XML payloads for SOAP or other XML-based endpoints from JSON examples
Convert JSON objects into XML with attributes by using the @_ key prefix
Quickly preview how a JSON structure maps to a nested XML tree

faq.q: Is my data sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser using JavaScript, and nothing you paste is uploaded or stored on any server.

faq.q: How do I create XML attributes instead of elements?
faq.a: Prefix the JSON key with @_, for example {"item": {"@_id": "1"}} becomes <item id="1">. Keys without the prefix become regular XML elements.
The XML is pretty-printed with two-space indentation, and trailing whitespace at the end is trimmed.

faq.q: What happens if my JSON is invalid?
faq.a: The input is parsed with JSON.parse, so malformed JSON throws a parse error and no XML is produced. Fix the JSON syntax and try again.

faq.q: Does it add an XML declaration or root wrapper?
faq.a: No declaration is added automatically, and the JSON structure is converted as-is. If your JSON has multiple top-level keys, wrap them in a single object key first to get one root element.
